title: U.S. House · West Virginia's 2nd District
area: West Virginia's 2nd Congressional District, covering the eastern panhandle and central/southern parts of the state including Charleston.

context.text: Incumbent Riley Moore (R) ran unopposed in the Republican primary. Ace Parsi won the Democratic primary on May 12, 2026.

summary.text: Riley Moore is the incumbent U.S. Representative for West Virginia's 2nd District, seeking re-election in 2026. A former welder and national security staffer, he served in the West Virginia House of Delegates and as West Virginia State Treasurer (2021-2025) before his election to Congress in 2024. He serves on the House Appropriations Committee.

background.text: A native of Morgantown, West Virginia, he lives in Harpers Ferry.
Began his career as a welder in a mining operation, according to his official biography.
Earned a bachelor's degree in government and international politics from George Mason University and a master's degree in strategic security studies from the National Defense University.

Worked as a national security staffer for the U.S. House Committee on Foreign Affairs, as a contract employee for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, and most recently in the defense and aerospace industry at Textron, according to his campaign website.

Elected in 2016 to the West Virginia House of Delegates from the 67th District, where he served as assistant majority whip and was named incoming Majority Leader in 2018; he lost his 2018 re-election bid.
Won the 2020 election for West Virginia State Treasurer over incumbent John Perdue and served as the state's 25th Treasurer from 2021 to 2025.

As Treasurer, he helped pass and administer the Hope Scholarship Program and the Jumpstart Savings Program; his official biography also says he divested West Virginia funds from BlackRock over the firm's support for ESG investing policies.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2024; sworn in January 3, 2025.

Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, on its Commerce, Justice, Science; Labor, Health and Human Services, Education; and Legislative Branch subcommittees. His campaign website also lists membership on the Elected Leadership Committee and the Whip team and says he leads the Republican Study Committee's Rescissions Task Force.
Lives in Harpers Ferry with his wife and their three children, according to his official biography.

positions.summary: In a 2025 op-ed he called for the largest deportation operation in American history and praised funding for expanded ICE detention capacity and more ICE agents.
positions.quote: President Trump needs to finish the wall and engage in the largest deportation operation in American history to undo the Biden border invasion.

positions.summary: After the Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed under IEEPA, he criticized the ruling and introduced the U.S. Reciprocal Trade Act to authorize the President to impose reciprocal tariffs.
positions.quote: The Court’s decision to strike down President Trump’s tariff policy is egregiously wrong, both as a matter of law and as a matter of justice for American workers.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Appropriations for the 119th Congress (2025-2026), including as Vice Chair of the Legislative Branch subcommittee, and to the Commerce-Justice-Science and Labor-HHS-Education subcommittees.

summary.text: Ace Parsi is a Morgantown community organizer and public education and democracy advocate running as the Democratic nominee for West Virginia's 2nd District. According to his campaign website, he was born in Iran, immigrated to the United States as a child and began his career as an AmeriCorps volunteer in a low-income school. He won the May 12, 2026 Democratic primary and says he is running on affordability, care and a more responsive government.

background.text: Born in Iran, he immigrated to the United States with his family at age eight, according to his campaign website and news coverage; he says his family relied on his brother's grocery job, his mother's sewing and child care work, and public assistance.
Describes learning English through English as a Second Language programs in public schools and becoming a high school state weightlifting record holder.

Earned a high school diploma from Wyoming Area High School and a bachelor's degree from Penn State University in 2005; The Dominion Post reports he later earned a graduate degree from the University of California, Berkeley.
Began his career as a teacher through AmeriCorps, serving in a low-income school.
Career experience includes working as an advocate on public education issues; news coverage describes him as a longtime community organizer and activist in Morgantown.
Announced his candidacy in January 2026 and won the May 12, 2026 Democratic primary with 39.8% of the vote over Stephanie Spears Tomana and Steven Wendelin.
Lives in Morgantown; married with a daughter, according to news coverage.

priorities.text: "We can have a more affordable future. By overturning the cuts in the Big Beautiful Bill, turning back tariffs on groceries, eliminating the current benefit cliffs... we can have that."
"We can have a more caring future. By investing in infrastructure around clean drinking water and investing in the individuals in care jobs whether they're nurses and teachers or law enforcement."

"We can have a more empowered future. We can take the power back from big tech and their AI imagined future and create systems and relationships where government and elected officials are more responsive."

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for ending the current tariffs and for Congress to exercise authority over them, while saying tariffs should be used to level the playing field.
positions.quote: Tariffs are taxes on consumers that have raised the prices for everything from ground beef to Christmas toys.

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for pursuing a single-payer public option and reversing Medicaid cuts in the 2025 budget law.
positions.quote: Healthcare: Fund rural hospitals; pursue a single-payer public option

positions.summary: His campaign platform lists raising the minimum wage to a living wage.
positions.quote: Raise the minimum wage to a living wage

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for tax incentives and zoning reform to build more housing.
positions.quote: Housing: Tax incentives and zoning reform to build more housing so West Virginians can afford to stay in West Virginia

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for redirecting funds lost to vouchers back into public schools.
positions.quote: redirect lost funds for vouchers back into public schools

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for diversifying energy supply through wind, solar and other sources and for cutting fossil fuel subsidies.
positions.quote: Energy: Diversify supply through wind, solar, and other sources to drive down heating bills
